title: Redwood discovery - model selection
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-10-06
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (Silverline CTO), Aisha Rahman (Silverline ML Lead), Luis Ortega (Silverline Infra), Rita Gomez (Silverline Product)
summary: Discovery focused on model selection across Redwood Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Customer needs: long context for multi-document summarization, robust multilingual support (EN/ES/FR), tool-calling for retrieval and custom API calls, and enterprise security (SAML, KMS). Discussed tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated vs private for latency, cost, and compliance; prioritized POC benchmarks for context length and throughput.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intro - I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood team, with Priya and Samir from our SE org. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Mark (Silverline CTO): Good, thanks. Mark here. we want to run through model selection, mainly focusing on long context and multilingual, and figure out fit for Hosted vs Dedicated or Private.
[00:18] Priya (Redwood SE): Awesome. high-level, we'll ask about workflows, latency targets, and data residency. Priya - I lead inference and deployment questions.
[00:25] Aisha (ML Lead): Hi - Aisha. Our main workload is multi-document summarization for legal and support docs. sometimes 50-200k tokens per session if you stitch multiple docs. we also need Spanish and French support.
[00:36] Luis (Infra): And we have SOC2 plus a few EU customers so data residency matters. leaning private for that, but cost is a concern.
[00:44] Jordan: Great. to orient: Redwood Hosted is fastest to get started, Dedicated gives committed capacity and isolation, Private gives you control for KMS/VPC/on-prem. we'll talk model choices - open models vs curated redwood variants, and features like tool-calling.
[00:58] Priya: Question - what are your latency SLOs? per-request vs streaming?
[01:03] Mark: For interactive tooling, sub-1s token latency would be ideal but we can tolerate a couple seconds for complex summarization. throughput for batch POCs matters - we might run 100 concurrent summarization jobs.
[01:15] Priya: Ok. for long contexts, there are two approaches - models with native long context (eg 32k or 64k) and retrieval+tool-calling where you short-context the model and call retrieval. both are supported. Redwood supports routing and KV cache for prefix reuse which helps cost.
[01:30] Aisha: We're leaning toward native long-context models for accuracy, since the summaries must keep document structure. any recommended open models?
[01:38] Samir: For native long context, open models like LlamaX-long* and Mistral-Long variants are options; they trade off cost/latency vs hallucination risk. we also have Redwood-verified profiles - we can share benchmark spreadsheets. note: some vendor model names get mis-typed in notes, but we'll attach the perf sheet.
[01:55] Luis: Tool-calling - we need the model to call our search API and a custodian metadata API. how mature is function-calling across models? any gotchas?
[02:03] Priya: Function-calling is broadly supported at the API layer. certain open models have better structure-output reliability. we recommend evaluating with your tool schemas; Redwood can run a short eval harness. sometimes you need light prompting and a post-parse step for small variations.
[02:18] Mark: Security questions - KMS for encryption, SSO (we use SAML), audit logs, and tenant isolation. If we go private, can we keep keys in our HSM?
[02:26] Jordan: Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC peering. Dedicated supports KMS integration but keys are managed differently. we'll share our security pack (SOC2, ISO artifacts).
[02:34] Aisha: On multilingual - models often degrade on non-English. which open models do well on Spanish and French?
[02:40] Samir: Mistral and some LlamaX configs do reasonably well. Also there are multilingual-specific open models (M2M-like) but with lower instruction-following. We recommend a two-pronged POC: run a multilingual eval set and measure ROUGE/semantic metrics.
[02:55] Rita (Product): For product: what's the dev experience like for tool-calls and streaming? we want to embed a streaming UI.
[03:01] Priya: Redwood API supports streaming, tool-calling, and structured response enforcement. streaming works across Hosted and Dedicated; in Private the same API is kept but you manage network.
[03:12] Mark: Cost - give us rough $/token differences hosted vs dedicated, and effect of quantization or 4-bit profiles.
[03:19] Jordan: High level: hosted has pay-as-you-go pricing; dedicated is cheaper per-token for sustained throughput. quantization and batching reduce cost significantly. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant profiles; we can produce ballpark numbers after we see your workload.
[03:34] Aisha: Do open models support quantization well? we've seen some regressions when going to 4-bit.
[03:40] Samir: Yes - quantization quality varies by model and architecture. part of the POC is a quality regression test suite. our runtime supports quant-friendly execution paths and will fall back to compatible kernels. occasionally tiny order-of-words changes happen - we'll flag them in diffs.
[03:56] [05:00] Jordan: quick demo note - we'll send a deck and a perf spreadsheet.
[05:03] Mark: Sounds good, yes please.
[05:06] Aisha: timeline: we want a pilot in Q4, ideally two-week POC, then expand.
[05:11] Jordan: Great. Suggested POC: 1) benchmark 32k vs retrieval+8k setup on your legal corpus, 2) tool-calling reliability tests with your search API, 3) multilingual eval on 500 doc sample. we'll run benchmarks on Hosted (fast) and Dedicated (to measure committed throughput), and if you need EU data residency we can scope Private.
[05:30] Luis: For infra, connectivity - what are egress requirements? we prefer VPC peering, no public egress for private data.
[05:36] Priya: Private supports VPC peering and can be air-gapped for on-prem. Dedicated supports VPC with restricted egress but depending on region there are options. we'll get your network checklist.
[05:48] Mark: Competitors - we are also talking to Anthropic and Cohere. also ran some tests with upstream LlamaX forks.
[05:56] Jordan: Noted. We'll include comparative notes but we'll focus the POC on models you care about.
[06:02] Aisha: Any constraints on tool-calling latency? sometimes we do a call per chunk and need 200-400ms addl latency.
[06:09] Priya: End-to-end depends on network and model. for Dedicated with local peering you can often get low added latency; Hosted in-region is usually OK too. we'll capture numbers in the perf sheet.
[06:20] [12:00] Mark: about context stitching - we want to preserve citation markers and section boundaries. do models maintain structured references well at 64k?
[12:09] Samir: In practice, quality at 64k varies by model; you may need prompt engineering and chunk-aware decoding. Another approach is hybrid: keep structure meta in the prompt and let the model reference via tool-calls to a retrieval layer for exact citations.
[12:26] Aisha: For evaluation metrics, we're going to use ROUGE + human QA for legal accuracy. can Redwood integrate our eval harness?
[12:34] Priya: Yes, we can ingest your evals, and Redwood Optimize can track regressions and alert. we'll need sample datasets.
[12:41] Rita: On compliance, how long are logs retained by default in Hosted? can we shorten?
[12:47] Jordan: Hosted defaults to 90 days but retention is configurable and longer retention is available as an add-on; Dedicated and Private give you more control.
[12:56] Luis: Regarding model updates - how do rollouts work? we don't want surprise changes in behavior.
[13:03] Priya: Redwood supports pinned model versions and rollout policies (canary, A/B). you can pin to a specific model/commit. we also surface token-level deltas in the console.
[13:15] Mark: Great. So next steps - we want pricing, security docs, and a POC plan.
[13:22] Jordan: We'll send a packet: perf spreadsheet, security pack, POC scope and template, and pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. propose a 2-week POC in your EU region to test residency.
[13:35] Aisha: Sounds good. Also please include recommended models for 64k native and for retrieval+8k fallback.
[13:43] Samir: We'll propose 2-3 model configs: 1) Mistral-Long-32k (native), 2) LlamaX-64k community build (native, if you accept tradeoffs), 3) Llama-instruct with retrieval + 8k context as fallback. plus quantized variants and profile notes.
[13:58] [40:00] Jordan: Ok quick recap: we'll share security artifacts, benchmarking sheet, proposed model list and POC plan + pricing. Action wise: Jordan to send pricing and POC template; Priya/Samir to run initial perf estimates and set up eval harness; Mark/Aisha to share sample docs and eval target metrics; Luis to share network checklist.
[40:20] Mark: I'll get the sample set uploaded to the secure bucket and share link.
[40:26] Aisha: I'll send the multilingual eval subset and the human QA rubric.
[40:30] Luis: I'll send the VPC and egress network checklist.
[40:33] Jordan: Thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invite for kickoff and set up SE-led benchmark run. Any final Qs?
[40:40] Rita: None from me. thanks.
[40:42] Jordan: Great - talk soon.
